title: Fed Decision in September?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's September 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for September 15-16, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their September meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

eventMetadata.context_description: Strong August 2026 employment data, with nonfarm payrolls surging 162,000 against lower expectations and labor force participation rising, has lifted trader odds for a 25 basis point federal funds rate increase at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting by underscoring labor market resilience. Incoming CPI and PPI readings scheduled for release shortly after will likely determine whether core price pressures justify tightening or support holding the 3.50-3.75% target range, given Chair Kevin Warsh’s emphasis on returning inflation to 2%. Hawkish signals from several policymakers contrast with comments from Governor Christopher Waller favoring patience if disinflation continues, while proximity to midterms adds caution against near-term moves. This balance of resilient jobs data against pending inflation prints and divided Fed views keeps the 25 basis point hike and no-change outcomes nearly even in the wisdom-of-crowds pricing.

eventMetadata.context_description: Eastern Michigan enters as a narrow home favorite against San Jose State in their first regular-season meeting, buoyed by a 28-17 Week 0 win over Sacramento State that showcased a stout defense limiting opponents to 271 total yards. The Spartans, coming off a 42-26 loss at USC where quarterback Luke Weaver threw for 234 yards and two touchdowns without turnovers while adding a rushing score, face back-to-back road games for the first time since 2011. Eastern Michigan’s Noah Kim posted 279 passing yards and two scores in the opener, while both teams rank competitively in early efficiency metrics. SJSU’s defense surrendered 505 yards to the Trojans, creating matchup questions at Rynearson Stadium amid limited injury concerns reported for either side.

eventMetadata.context_description: Lula leads the 2026 Brazilian presidential race as the incumbent seeking re-election, though recent Datafolha and other polls show his first-round support at 38% against Flávio Bolsonaro’s 33%, with the gap narrowing sharply after the start of free electoral broadcasts and televised debates. In runoff simulations, the contest has tightened to a statistical tie around 46-44, reflecting high rejection rates for both frontrunners and the impact of economic headwinds including weak household consumption. Flávio’s positioning benefits from his father Jair Bolsonaro’s endorsement despite the former president’s legal barriers, while Augusto Cury’s rapid rise to 8% highlights vote fragmentation on the right. Trader consensus on Polymarket prices these polling trends and campaign momentum as the primary drivers heading into the October first round.

eventMetadata.context_description: Several elite clubs enter the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League with comparable title credentials, producing tightly bunched implied probabilities among Barcelona, Arsenal, Bayern Munich, Paris Saint-Germain, and Real Madrid. PSG seek a historic three-peat after back-to-back triumphs, bolstered by attacking depth featuring Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and summer additions, yet early domestic results have tempered momentum. Arsenal arrive with momentum from an unbeaten league-phase run and final appearance last season, while Bayern’s potent attack led by Harry Kane and Barcelona’s domestic dominance keep them in the mix. The new Swiss-format league phase, challenging draw pairings, and squad reinforcements across contenders sustain parity, as no side has separated decisively heading into matchday one.
